reason: RespawnPack's own killed-feature contract — the pack dogfooding kernel/lib/removals.js against itself. Every row below is a decision this repository has ALREADY made and recorded, with the citation in `evidence`; none is invented to give the scanner something to do. ⛔ THIS SET IS A FLOOR, NOT AN INVENTORY: a removal is only guarded once it has a row here naming the phrases that would reintroduce it, so anything retired from here on needs a row at the time it is retired, not at the next audit. `respawnpack removals` prints which rows are guarded and which are `unverified` — read it rather than assuming the absolute holds.

removals.reason: Retired 2026-08-07 (CHANGELOG, 'the assumed context window is 1M, not 200k'). The context-pressure signal measured every session against an assumed 200,000-token window while every current Opus and Sonnet has 1M — a denominator wrong by 5x on essentially every real session, which crossed mandatory handoff at ~170k tokens with 830k still free. A warning that is always wrong is one that gets turned off. `RESPAWNPACK_CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS` now defaults to 1000000 in hooks/context-monitor.js, hooks/precompact-ledger-nudge.js and adapters/claude-code/sdk-supervisor/measure.js.
removals.evidence: CHANGELOG.md § Changed — the assumed context window is 1M, not 200k (2026-08-07)

removals.reason: Replaced by the per-context-cycle latch with re-arm on observed compaction. The old latch was keyed by session id, and a compacted conversation KEEPS its session id — so each threshold fired once in the life of a conversation and went silent for every cycle after it, leaving the third session, the one that most needed a checkpoint, with nothing. ⛔ This row is the one in this registry with a proven drift history: hooks/README.md was still describing the per-session latch as current behaviour after the re-arm replaced it, and that is the only reason the defect was found. A prose-level resurrection here is not hypothetical.
removals.evidence: CHANGELOG.md § Fixed (2026-08-07), '`hooks/README.md` still described the v0.2 per-session latch, which the per-cycle re-arm replaced'; hooks/README.md ⛔ note under context-monitor.js

removals.feature: separate packages, a second repository, or a plugin architecture for the core/optional boundary
removals.reason: Decided against in ADR-002 (accepted 2026-08-05). The finding was that `core vs optional packs` had no artifact anywhere in the repository, and that leaving it open invited someone to INVENT one — to build a plugin loader, split the repository, or publish separate packages so the boundary had something to point at. The decision is that the mechanisms already exist: RespawnPack ships as one pack with four axes of optionality already in the installer. A plugin loader is a new trust boundary and a new failure mode bought for nothing.

removals.feature: file-backed memory described as a degraded fallback
removals.reason: A killed FRAMING rather than a killed module, and it belongs here for the same reason a killed feature does: the claim is false and the repository has committed to not making it. ADR-002 states it as a guarantee — file-backed memory is CORE, not a degraded fallback. kernel/lib/memory.js returns `mode: 'file'` with the detail 'the zero-setup default', and doctor reports `memory:distribution ACTIVE` on a default install. ADR-002's own words: the word 'degraded' appears nowhere on that path, because it would be false. The memory engine (`--with-memory`) is an optional enhancement, and prose that inverts this tells a founder they have half a product when they have all of it.

removals.feature: the skip-branch quality gate, and NOT_APPLICABLE inferred from an empty search
removals.reason: Retired with kernel/lib/gate.js. `templates/ci/quality-gate.yml` ran four steps — lint, typecheck, test, build — each guarded by its own skip branch, so on a repo with no Node lockfile every one printed 'skipping' and the job reported GREEN: a workflow named 'quality gate' reporting success having run zero checks, on exactly the projects the installer already knew were Python, mixed, or monorepos. ⛔ AND BETTER SKIP MESSAGES WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT — the failure was never the wording, it was that nothing computed an OUTCOME, and a skipped step exits 0. The gate is now a program returning a verdict. This is the pack's flagship defect class, which is why it is high risk: NOT_APPLICABLE is only ever DECLARED, never inferred, and 'I looked and found nothing' is NOT_CONFIGURED — the honest answer, and not green.
removals.evidence: kernel/lib/gate.js header, ⛔ THE DEFECT THIS REPLACES and the ⭐ NOT_APPLICABLE rule

removals.reason: Retired with the three-tier push range in hooks/secret-scan.js. The old fallback chain ended at `HEAD~1..HEAD`, so on a NEW BRANCH WITH NO UPSTREAM — the single most common shape for 'about to push for the first time' — the scan saw only the newest commit, a secret introduced three commits back shipped clean, and the hook reported success. High risk because this row guards a SECURITY BACKSTOP's stated coverage: prose that understates the range is a reader trusting a narrower scan than they have, and prose that restates the retired range is a reader trusting a scan that already failed once.
removals.evidence: hooks/secret-scan.js ⛔ THE RANGE DEFECT THIS REPLACES; hooks/README.md secret-scan diff-range note

removals.feature: the derived-doc migration described as irreversible
removals.reason: A killed LIMITATION, and it belongs here for the same reason a killed feature does: the claim is now false and repeating it reproduces the original defect. `savepoint --verify --write` archives CONTINUITY.md/GAPS.md and rewrites them, and because that was a door with no way back, it was not something an owner would meet for the first time at closeout — so exit 2 was permanent and THE MIGRATION NEVER RAN. v0.3 added `restore-derived` (render.js planRestore): preview by default, `--write` performs it, the archive is never deleted, and migrate -> restore -> migrate all resolve to the same original. ⛔ 'one-way door' is deliberately NOT a forbidden phrase here: it is standard architecture vocabulary and agents/system-architect.md uses it correctly about datastore decisions. A phrase that collides with innocent prose produces a real FAIL and teaches operators to scroll past this check.
removals.evidence: CHANGELOG.md § Fixed — the 2026-08-07 field run punch list (2026-08-07), the derived-doc migration item

removals.feature: the installer seeding a placeholder string as a config value
removals.reason: Retired 2026-08-12 (commit 5204353, CHANGELOG 'an unfinished onboarding says so'). install.js seeded routeSource='<set ROUTE_SOURCE>' and codeTruth='<set CODE_TRUTH: token/copy/schema source paths>' as literal VALUES, and /savepoint's routes step enumerates that value against FEATURES-PAGES.md - handed a template it globs zero routes, finds zero orphans in both directions, and reports no drift. A check that matches nothing agrees with everything. An undetected value now writes NO KEY, and an absent key is UNDECIDED. ⛔ THIS ROW EXISTS BECAUSE IT WAS OWED AND MISSING: the commit that retired the behaviour added no row, which is the one obligation this registry's own reason field says must be met at retirement time rather than at the next audit. It is the recorded instance of P-022 in docs/derived/state/pairs.json.
removals.evidence: CHANGELOG.md § Added — an unfinished onboarding says so, instead of wearing a broken project's clothes (2026-08-12); install/install.js routeSource initialisation; kernel/lib/applicability.js INSTALLER_TEMPLATE

rejectedPhrases.why: ⛔ REJECTED: it flags the PROHIBITION. spine/reference/testing-standards.md rule 15 reads 'Installers write no key rather than a placeholder value' — correct prose stating the very rule, which this phrase would report as a live reintroduction. Same class as the two candidate rows this registry already rejected: when the prohibition's vocabulary IS the anti-pattern's name, a row on that vocabulary teaches operators to scroll past the check, which costs more than the row is worth. Verified empirically before removal, not reasoned about: the candidate FAILED against testing-standards.md:53.

⛔ REJECTED for the same reason, at four sites: skills/savepoint/SKILL.md, skills/onboard/SKILL.md and its .base.md twin, all of which quote the literal in order to say it is INVALID and never read as a value. A row cannot guard a template by matching the template, because the documentation that retires it has to name it.
